writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 152 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
It is believed that teachers can exert a profound influence on their students' academic pursuit and personal development. Having spent years in classrooms, I firmly agree that a dedicated teacher shapes not only what we learn but also who we become.
On the one hand, teachers guide our academic growth. My high-school chemistry teacher, Mr. Li, turned a subject I once dreaded into my favourite one. By designing vivid experiments and patiently answering my endless questions, he inspired me to pursue science and eventually major in it at university. On the other hand, teachers mould our character. Through his fairness and honesty, Mr. Li taught me to value integrity over easy shortcuts, a lesson that still steers my decisions today.
In conclusion, a good teacher enlightens the mind and cultivates the heart at the same time. Their influence, though quiet and gradual, reaches far beyond examinations and often lasts a whole lifetime.

lines.en: W: I must say, I love our canteen! It's such a great meeting point!
lines.zh: W: 我得说，我太喜欢我们的食堂了！那里真是个很棒的碰面地点！

lines.en: M: Yeah, it really is, both for students and teachers. Shame about the food.
lines.zh: M: 是啊，对学生和老师来说确实都是这样。就是食物有点可惜。

lines.en: W: What do you mean? I think the food is fine.
lines.zh: W: 你这是什么意思？我觉得食物还不错啊。

lines.en: M: I would say the food is just OK, but the prices are absurd. Don't you agree?
lines.zh: M: 我觉得食物只能算还行，但价格实在离谱。你不这么认为吗？

lines.en: W: I don't, actually. I personally think they're perfectly appropriate. If it's overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunchtimes?
lines.zh: W: 其实我不这么认为。我个人觉得价格完全合理。如果价格过高，为什么午餐时间那里会忙得不可开交呢？

lines.en: M: Hmm, you make a good point. I guess a lot of it is good value, maybe even most of it. However, don't you think 6 bucks for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students' budgets?
lines.zh: M: 嗯，你说得有道理。我想其中很多食物都很划算，甚至大多数都很划算。不过，你不觉得一片苹果酥要6块钱，超出了大多数学生的预算吗？

lines.en: W: Um, yes, desserts are overpriced. I'll give you that. To be honest, I've forgotten about those, as I never eat them. I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies. What I always go for is their scrambled eggs. They have such a great variety.
lines.zh: W: 嗯，是的，甜点确实定价过高。这点我同意。说实话，我都忘了那些甜点，因为我从来不吃。我从来不会特别想吃甜食或什么精致的美味。我每次都会选他们的炒鸡蛋。他们提供的种类真多。

lines.en: M: Yeah, those are good. They also come out really fast. Actually, that's one of the best things about the canteen — the speed. If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don't have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option. The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace. They really deserve to be complimented for it.
lines.zh: M: 是啊，那些炒鸡蛋很好吃。而且出餐速度也很快。其实，这是食堂最棒的地方之一——速度。如果我想吃点比三明治更实在的东西，但午餐时间又不多，大学食堂总是个不错的选择。厨房工作人员干活特别利索。他们真的应该因此受到表扬。

lines.en: W: Totally, and it's such a great environment too. Like the entire building is beautiful.
lines.zh: W: 完全同意，而且那里的环境也特别好。整个建筑都很漂亮。

lines.en: M: It is very nice.
lines.zh: M: 确实很不错。

lines.en: W: The massive glass windows make all the difference. I think they're so cool. Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago. It cost them a pretty penny.
lines.zh: W: 那些巨大的玻璃窗让整个地方完全不一样。我觉得它们特别酷。听说他们几年前进行了一次大规模翻修，花了不少钱。

lines.en: M: Yeah, I'm not surprised. It's a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing.
lines.zh: M: 是啊，我一点也不意外。那是个用途非常灵活的空间，既适合吃饭，也适合放松。

lines.en: W: And for working.
lines.zh: W: 也适合工作。

lines.en: M: You're right, working too. I've used my laptop there once or twice. And there's always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.
lines.zh: M: 你说得对，也适合工作。我在那里用过一两次笔记本电脑。而且远端总是有小组项目或会议在进行。

transcripts.head: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

lines.en: W: Hi, Tony, today we're talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work. We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic. That's not really justified though, is it?
lines.zh: W: 嗨，托尼，今天我们来谈谈管理者如何在工作中更好地与年轻人相处。我们经常听到有人说，如今的年轻人职业道德较差。不过，这种说法其实并没有什么依据，对吧？

lines.en: M: Not really. In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
lines.zh: M: 确实没有。实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样，都是多种多样、各具特点的。

lines.en: W: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
lines.zh: W: 是的，但如果你在工作中和年轻人合作时遇到了困难，你能做些什么呢？

lines.en: M: Well, it's essential to connect with them to learn about their values. It's also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
lines.zh: M: 首先，必须与他们建立联系，了解他们的价值观。同样重要的是，要认识到年轻人希望如何平衡工作与个人生活。

lines.en: W: So they generally don't want to defer happiness in return for career advancement?
lines.zh: W: 所以，他们通常不想为了事业发展而推迟享受生活？

lines.en: M: Absolutely. They are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
lines.zh: M: 完全正确。他们不愿意为了工作生活而牺牲个人生活，而这就导致人们把这种态度等同于不愿意努力工作。

lines.en: W: Right. But that couldn't be further from the truth, could it?
lines.zh: W: 没错。但事实完全不是这样，对吧？

lines.en: M: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights free from work.
lines.zh: M: 年轻人在规定的工作时间内会非常努力地工作，但他们希望自己的休息时间，比如周末和晚上，不受工作打扰。

lines.en: W: So how should managers go about assessing young people's productivity?
lines.zh: W: 那么，管理者应该如何评估年轻人的工作效率呢？

lines.en: M: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company. Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
lines.zh: M: 总的来说，年轻人认为，工作效率不应该用工作时长来衡量，因为有人可能工作八个小时，却几乎没有为公司完成任何有意义的事情。相反，年轻人会根据自己完成的工作质量来衡量工作效率。

lines.en: W: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine. Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can't it?
lines.zh: W: 但我们经常听到，年轻人希望感受到的不只是自己属于一台庞大机器的一部分。这种观点很难反驳，对吧？

lines.en: M: It's important to legitimize their work. Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company or the world at large. They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
lines.zh: M: 认可他们工作的价值很重要。年轻人希望参与对自己、公司或整个世界都有意义的项目。他们必须觉得，公司所秉持的价值观与自己的价值观一致，这样才愿意继续在那里工作。

lines.en: W: Thanks for your advice.
lines.zh: W: 谢谢你的建议。

lines.en: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes. Although it sounds counter-intuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
lines.zh: 许多餐厅正试图劝说顾客以更可持续的方式饮食，从对环境不友好的肉类转向更环保的菜肴。一项新研究表明，尽管这听起来有悖直觉，但菜单上设有专门素食菜品区的餐厅可能会在无意中鼓励顾客食用肉类。

lines.en: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study's authors, said, "Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat. However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others." The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it. No vegetarians were included. They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends. Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters. But it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65%. The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef's recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option. But again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
lines.zh: 行为科学家琳达·培根是该研究的作者之一，她说：“餐厅可以通过鼓励顾客选择更多植物性食物、少吃肉类，对环境产生积极影响。然而，我们的研究结果表明，某些餐厅菜单设计虽然能促使一些消费者作出有利于环境的食物选择，却可能对另一些消费者产生相反的效果。”这项研究涉及750人，其中一半经常吃素食，另一半很少吃素食。参与者中没有素食者。他们拿到不同的菜单，并被要求像和朋友外出就餐一样选择一顿饭。将素食菜品放在单独的栏目中，对很少吃素食者的选择没有显著影响。但这一做法对经常吃素食者产生了明显影响，使他们选择素食菜品的可能性降低了65%。研究人员还发现，将一道素食菜品列为主厨推荐，或为一道非肉类餐食附上更具吸引力的描述，会使选择素食菜品的不常吃素食者比例更高。但同样，这些经过调整的菜单设计对经常吃素食者适得其反，使他们更不可能选择素食菜品。

lines.en: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors. They found that if pollution is frozen to around –18 ℃ in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through. Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants. It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
lines.zh: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在努力寻找一种方法，防止致命的室外空气污染渗入室内。他们发现，如果在冷凝管中将污染物冷冻至约−18℃，颗粒物就会聚集在一起并落到底部，从而使新鲜、洁净的空气通过。他们的方法能够去除99%的污染物。人们希望，这项工作能够为简单改造空调设备铺平道路，使其也能清洁受到污染的室内空气。

lines.en: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Calcutta or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools. While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive or produce harmful by-products. When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors. But outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer. It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year. Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, "We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants. Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions. By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health."
lines.zh: 城市室外空气污染是一个全球性问题，无论是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校儿童健康的恶劣空气，都是如此。虽然目前已有一些净化室内空气的技术，但它们可能效率低下、成本高昂，或产生有害副产品。当室外空气质量较差时，人们往往会在室内待更长时间。但室外污染也会导致室内污染，人们仍然会受到影响。据估计，在英国，污染每年与4万多例过早死亡有关。中国科学院的潘刚教授说：“我们的实验表明，只需让受污染的空气循环通过一个小型冷冻室，就能去除大部分细颗粒物和气态污染物。我们的研究使得在可能经历极差空气状况的地区，为家用电器增加空气净化功能成为可能。通过以这种方式控制室内空气污染并改善空气质量，这项工作将大大有益于公众健康。”

lines.en: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware. A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
lines.zh: 我的团队最近开展的研究表明，鱼类可能具有自我意识。最近，有一种鱼通过了著名的镜子测试。

lines.en: This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals. Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins and some birds, can recognize themselves in a mirror. And only these animals, capable of self-recognition, will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection. This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness. This is not shown by children until around 18 months. Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability. But our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror. The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out. The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present or when the marks were just placed on the mirror. Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window. These results show either that fish are self-aware or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
lines.zh: 这是一项用来证明动物具有自我识别能力的测试。只有少数动物，例如人类、猿类、海豚和一些鸟类，能够在镜子中认出自己。也只有这些具有自我识别能力的动物，才会在倒影中注意到皮肤上的标记后，试图将其去除。这种能力表明动物具有较高程度的智力和意识。儿童要到大约18个月大时才会表现出这种能力。到目前为止，还没有鱼类展示过这种能力。但我们的实验表明，这种鱼在镜子中看到自己后，会在坚硬的表面上摩擦身体，以去除研究人员放在它身上的标记。我们观察到的行为几乎毫无疑问地表明，这种鱼在行为上满足了镜子测试最初设定的全部标准。我们的研究中的鱼在没有镜子时，或标记只是被放在镜子上时，从未试图去除这些标记。未被标记的鱼在隔着窗户与另一侧的被标记鱼互动时，也没有试图去除自己身上的标记。这些结果表明，要么鱼类具有自我意识，要么被视为判定较高智力的黄金标准测试的镜子测试存在缺陷。

lines.en: What is less clear is whether these behaviors should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past these same behaviors have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals. Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviors in a fish satisfy passing the test at all. But on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviors they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
lines.zh: 不太明确的是，尽管过去人们一直将其他许多动物的这些相同行为解释为自我意识的表现，但这些行为是否应被视为鱼类具有自我意识的证据。根据你的立场，你可能完全拒绝接受这样的解释，即鱼类的这些行为足以满足通过该测试的条件。但是，当鱼类表现出的行为在功能上与其他通过测试的物种如此相似时，你又能以什么客观依据这样做呢？

lines.en: Results from our research raise more questions than answers. What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer rather than appearing all at once? Perhaps in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test. Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
lines.zh: 我们的研究结果提出的问题多于给出的答案。如果自我意识像洋葱一样逐层发展，而不是一下子全部出现，会怎么样？也许，为了进一步探究自我意识，我们应该不再把对镜子的反应视为决定性测试。只有建立起更丰富的自我理论，并采用规模更大的测试组合，我们才能确定自我意识的各种不同层次，包括鱼类究竟处于其中的哪个位置。

lines.en: Reading with a young child is important. But does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print? As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens. So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more.
lines.zh: 与年幼的孩子一起阅读很重要。但从电子书还是传统纸质书阅读，这一点是否有区别呢？正如任何家长都知道的那样，幼儿通常都很喜欢屏幕。因此，一项新研究发现，幼儿更喜欢电子书而不是纸质图画书，这或许并不令人十分意外——但接下来的附加发现可能会让人感到意外：家长和孩子在阅读电子图画书与纸质图画书时的行为有所不同。而且，阅读电子书的孩子学到了更多内容。

lines.en: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print. In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books. But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
lines.zh: 此前针对幼儿的研究表明，电子书加入了词典、描绘故事情节的图片等额外功能，因此可能比纸质书更具优势。事实上，多项研究发现，电子书在促进故事理解和词汇增长方面，所起的作用超出了纸质书所能提供的效果。但也有研究表明，孩子有时在从电子书中学习时投入的脑力较少，而且家长与孩子共同阅读电子书时，对内容谈论得也比较少。

lines.en: The study we're looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children. For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents. Each parent-child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content. While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
lines.zh: 我们今天要了解的这项研究，旨在帮助我们更好地理解电子书对幼儿究竟有多大益处。在这项研究中，研究人员拍摄了17至26个月大的孩子与其中一位家长共同阅读的过程。每一对家长和孩子被随机分配阅读两本教育类电子书，或两本内容相同的纸质书。家长大声朗读纸质书中的文字，而电子书则配有配音演员朗读文本的音频。

lines.en: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books. But the opposite was true for the children. Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
lines.zh: 研究人员发现，阅读纸质书的家长比阅读电子书的家长更频繁地指向书页。但孩子的情况正好相反。阅读电子书的孩子还会更多地评论书中内容，并且比阅读纸质书的孩子学会更多新词。

lines.en: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books. It's important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple. While they included background music, animation and sound effects, there were no other extra features.
lines.zh: 这种更好的学习效果被归因于孩子对电子书更高的参与度。需要注意的是，这项研究中的电子书很简单。虽然其中包含背景音乐、动画和音效，但没有其他额外功能。

lines.en: It's also important to note that there's research on older children, finding that electronic books don't always bolster learning. Parents and educators need to beware. Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
lines.zh: 同样需要注意的是，针对年龄较大儿童的研究发现，电子书并不总能促进学习。家长和教育工作者需要对此保持警惕。电子书中的额外功能可能会提高孩子对电子书的参与度；然而，如果这些功能不能将孩子的注意力吸引到教育内容上，那么它们可能就无法起到支持作用。

lines.en: Let me be honest with you. If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time. Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today? There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No!
lines.zh: 让我坦诚地告诉你。如果你满怀悔恨地生活，就是在浪费时间。你为什么要在一生中不断后悔那些造就了今天的你的决定呢？我们做过许多不利的决定，但这是否意味着我们应该后悔？不！

lines.en: I've had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently. However, just because things could be different, it doesn't necessarily mean they would be better. You don't have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one. You can't go back and change anything, so what's the point in worrying about it?
lines.zh: 我曾有过许多时候，坐下来思考所有那些我希望自己能够做得不同的事情。然而，仅仅因为事情本可以有所不同，并不一定意味着结果会更好。你不必一直思考过去所做的每一个决定，以及自己是否做出了正确的选择。你无法回到过去改变任何事情，那么又何必为此担忧呢？

lines.en: Every single decision you've ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today. We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that? We would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
lines.zh: 你曾经做出的每一个决定，无论积极还是消极，都造就了今天的你。我们想回到过去，改变过去的一些部分，但那样做会有什么益处呢？我们会失去从所学教训中获得的宝贵知识。

lines.en: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are. So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself. Because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
lines.zh: 你所做的每个选择都有其原因，而这些原因体现了你是怎样的人。因此，当你面对人生中的任何决定时，都要毫不 apologetically 地做自己。因为归根结底，是你做出了那个决定。

lines.en: With less time spent focused on regrets, you'll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life. In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make. Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can't let regret stop us from moving forward.
lines.zh: 少花些时间专注于悔恨，你终于会有时间去关注生活中更重要的事情。在任何情况下，你都会随着自己做出的每一个决定而不断成长。生活充满了值得学习的教训，所以我们不能让悔恨阻止我们继续前进。

lines.en: We don't know if we've made the right or wrong choice until after it's already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision. But if the decision has already been made, what's the purpose of dwelling on it? There isn't one. All you can do is move forward. You can't let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice. We aren't all perfect.
lines.zh: 在一个选择已经做出之前，我们不知道它究竟是正确的还是错误的，所以很容易开始后悔自己的决定。但如果决定已经做出，反复纠结它又有什么意义呢？没有任何意义。你能做的只有继续向前。你不能让自己坐在那里，为过去做出的每一个选择忧虑不已。我们都不可能完美。

lines.en: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later, but that's how life is supposed to be. You will make poor decisions in life — we all do — but it's what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
lines.zh: 每当你做出一个决定，之后总有可能产生悔恨，但人生本来就应该是这样。你会在人生中做出糟糕的决定——我们都会如此——但真正重要的是，你如何对待从中吸取的教训。

lines.en: Think about every decision you've ever made. Were they always the best? Of course not. But look at how far you've come since then.
lines.zh: 想想你曾经做出的每一个决定。它们是否总是最好的？当然不是。但看看从那时起你已经走了多远。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise?

analysis.定位: P1 So the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise — but the following additional findings might: both parents and children behaved differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books. And the children who read the electronic books learned more. 因此，一项新研究发现幼儿比起纸质图画书更喜欢电子书，这一点也许并不令人意外——但接下来这些额外发现就可能令人意外了：父母和孩子在读电子书与纸质书时表现各不相同；而且读电子书的孩子学到的更多。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What do we learn about previous studies of young children reading electronic books?
questions.stem_zh: 关于幼儿阅读电子书的以往研究，我们了解到什么？

analysis.信号: but 把两拨研究结论正反对置。录音先说 multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains（电子书有利），再用 But there's also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort（也有研究说不利）一转，正反两拨研究结论摆在一起——这正是"结论相互矛盾"的信号。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children's learning?
questions.stem_zh: 电子书中应加入哪些额外功能来促进儿童学习？

analysis.定位: P6 Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them; however, if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature. 电子书里的额外功能也许能提高孩子的参与度；然而，如果这些功能不能把注意力引向教育内容，它们就可能起不到辅助作用。

analysis.替换: if these features don't draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature↔Those that draw their attention to the educational content否定条件转正面、原词点对
analysis.排除: A)原词陷阱Those that prove simple enough for them to comprehend. 蹭了第 5 段 the electronic books in the study were simple 的 simple，但那只是描述研究所用电子书的特点，录音从没说"简单到能懂"是促进学习该加的功能，听到 simple 就选会落坑。 借用原文：the electronic books in the study were simple B)原词陷阱Those that produce both audio and visual effects on them. 直接搬录音 they included background music, animation and sound effects 的音乐、动画、音效，这些恰是"声光效果"，但录音的落点是"光有这些额外功能、若不指向教育内容就没用"，B 把被否定的诱饵当成了答案。 借用原文：they included background music, animation and sound effects D)偷换概念Those that contribute to their increased interest in reading. 像是改写自录音 Extra features…may increase children's participation，但录音说的是 increase participation（提高参与度），并把它和"促进学习"区分开（参与高未必学得好），选项把它换成 increased interest in reading（提高阅读兴趣）且当成促学习的条件，偷换且跑题。 借用原文：Extra features in electronic books may increase children's participation with them

questions.stem: 【题目】 What should we do with the unfavorable decisions we've made?

analysis.定位: P1 If you're living your life full of regrets, you're wasting your time. ... There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we've made, but does that mean we should regret them? No! 如果你的人生充满后悔，那就是在浪费时间。……我们确实做过很多不理想的决定，但这是否意味着我们该为之后悔呢？不！

cloze.title: 2025年12月·第2套 英语六级完形填空（选词填空） · 26–35 题答案与解析

passages.en: We humans love to believe we are special, but science and technology have repeatedly proved this conviction wrong. People __(26)__ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things.
passages.zh: 我们人类喜欢相信自己与众不同，但科学和技术一再证明这种信念是错误的。人们曾经认为，人类是唯一会使用工具、组建团队或传播文化的动物，但科学已经表明，其他动物也会做这些事情。

passages.en: Meanwhile, technology has quashed(使无效), one by one, claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain. The first adding machine was invented in 1623. This past year, a computer-generated work won an art contest. I believe the moment when computers meet and __(28)__ human intelligence is on the horizon.
passages.zh: 与此同时，技术逐一使那些认为认知任务需要人类大脑才能完成的说法失去了依据。第一台加法机于1623年发明。就在过去一年，一件由计算机生成的作品赢得了一场艺术比赛。我相信，计算机达到并超越人类智能的时刻已经近在眼前。

passages.en: How will human intelligence and creativity be valued when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people? There will likely be a spectrum. In some __(29)__ , people still value humans doing things, even if a computer can do it better. It's been a quarter of a century since a computer beat world champion Garry Kasparov, but human chess hasn't gone away.
passages.zh: 当机器变得比最聪明的人更聪明、更有创造力时，人类的智慧和创造力将如何受到重视？情况很可能会呈现出一个连续谱。在某些领域，即使计算机能做得更好，人们仍然重视由人类亲自完成的事情。计算机击败世界冠军加里·卡斯帕罗夫已经过去四分之一个世纪，但人类国际象棋并没有因此消失。

passages.en: In other fields, human skill will seem costly and __(30)__ . Take illustration for example: most readers don't care whether the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer — they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __(32)__ .
passages.zh: 在其他领域，人类的技能将显得昂贵而且多余。以插画为例：大多数读者并不在意杂志文章配图究竟是由人还是计算机绘制的，他们只希望配图切合内容、新颖，也许还要有趣。

passages.en: And, of course, this question isn't black or white. Many fields will be a __(33)__ , where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines.
passages.zh: 当然，这个问题并不是非黑即白的。许多领域将呈现人机融合的状态：少数人找到一个幸运的位置，但大部分工作由计算机完成。如今的制造业就是如此，大量工作由机器人完成，但仍然必须有一些人在场监督机器。

passages.en: If history is any guide, it's almost certain that advances in AI will cause more jobs to __(35)__ , that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number, and that those who own creative technology will become the new ultra-rich.
passages.zh: 如果历史可以作为借鉴，那么人工智能的发展几乎必然会导致更多工作岗位消失；拥有只有人类才能具备的技能的创意工作者会变得更加富有，但人数会减少；而拥有创意技术的人将成为新一代超级富豪。

wordbank.gloss: 伴随的；陪伴（现在分词/动名词，可作定语修饰名词）
认知的；与思维/智力相关的
曾经；从前（也可作连词，但此处取副词义）
多余的；被裁掉的；不再需要的

rows.text: I) once副词
主语与谓语之间的状语位

与 but 后的 has shown 构成今昔对比 People __(26)__ thought that humans were the only animals to use tools, to form teams or to propagate culture, but science has shown that other animals do each of these things. 前半句过去时 thought、后半句现在完成时 has shown，典型 "过去曾以为 / 如今已证明" 结构，填 once（曾经）正好咬合这条时间逻辑。
N)tentatively语义指向不对，是 "试探性地" 而非 "曾经" tentatively 意为 "暂时地、试探性地"，强调态度不坚定。但原文说人们 "长久以为人类是唯一会用工具的动物"，这是一种**坚信**而非试探，与下句被 but 反转的语气不匹配。
B) cognitive形容词
名词 tasks 前的前置定语

与 "require a human brain" 同义呼应 claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain——能 require a human brain（需要人脑）的任务，正是 cognitive tasks（认知性的任务、需要思维加工的任务）。下一句又用 adding machine、computer-generated art、computer matches human intelligence 反复指向 "智力/认知"，B 与上下文构成最稳同义网。

H)intuitive"直觉的" 与 "人脑认知" 范围不符 intuitive 指 "凭直觉的"，强调非理性、不依靠分析。而本段下文举例（加法机、AI 绘画、计算机匹敌人类智能）恰恰是**理性认知**任务被机器接管，与 intuitive 的语义指向相反。 D)entertaining"有趣的" 偏娱乐，与 "需要人脑" 不沾边 entertaining 指 "令人愉快的、有娱乐性的"，与 require a human brain（需要人脑）这一论点完全脱节，纯属词性诱饵。 K)redundant"多余的任务" 与原意南辕北辙 redundant 是 "多余的、被裁掉的"——"多余的任务需要人脑" 在逻辑上根本说不通；况且 K 后文 30 题正等着它。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 H) —— 看到 AI 话题就联想 "直觉"。intuitive 词性对、又与 AI 话题表面沾边（"机器没有直觉"），最易让考生误填。防坑：claims that __(27)__ tasks require a human brain 里同句锚词是 a human brain，"需要人脑的任务" = cognitive（认知性的），而非 intuitive（直觉的）。"找同句同义锚" 是六级选词填空的必修招式。
M) surpass动词
and 并列谓语：computers meet and __ human intelligence

"匹敌并超越" 是 AI 论述的固定搭配 I believe the moment when computers meet and __(28)__ human intelligence is on the horizon.——meet（达到/匹敌）+ surpass（超越）是 AI 话题里最常见的递进搭配，且呼应第三段 when machines become smarter and more creative than the brightest people（变得比最聪明的人更聪明、更有创造力），证实方向就是 "超越"。
C) domains名词
介词 In some 后的名词复数

"在某些领域里" 与下文 In other fields 形成对照 下一段开头 In other fields, human skill will seem costly and __(30)__. 用 In other fields 与本段 In some __(29)__ 形成 "在某些领域 / 在另一些领域" 的并列对照；domains（领域）与 fields 同义，正好咬合这条段间对照逻辑。

L)stances"立场" 与下文 fields 不对应 stances 指 "立场、姿态"，是抽象观点。但下段 in other fields 明确把对比维度定在 "领域" 而非 "立场"——填 stances 会让段间对照失锚。 G)impetus形态不对：单数且不可数 impetus 通常作不可数单数（推动力），与 some + 复数名词的结构不合；语义上 "在某些推动力里人们仍重视人类" 也不通。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 L) —— 复数名词形态一致的假同义。stances 与 domains 同为复数名词、同能套进 In some __ 结构，最易混。防坑：盯紧下段段首 In other fields——"领域 vs 立场" 是两条线，fields 同义对应 domains。"段间对照锁名词" 一招直接破。
K) redundant形容词
并列连词 and 后接形容词，与 costly 并列

"昂贵 + 多余" 共同描述被淘汰的人类技能 本段例 most readers don't care whether the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer——读者并不在意是人画的还是机器画的，意味着人类技能既贵又**没必要**，redundant（多余的、被裁掉的）正好把这层负面评价点透。
D)entertaining褒义色彩与 costly 不同向 entertaining（有趣的）偏褒，而 costly 偏负面——并列时色彩不一致，逻辑上 "昂贵且有趣" 也无法描述被市场淘汰的人类劳动。 H)intuitive"直觉的" 与 "被淘汰" 主线不沾 intuitive 指 "直觉的"，并不直接传递价值高低、是否被取代的信息，与本段 "人类技能将变得不值" 的论点错位。
A) accompanying形容词
the graphic __ a magazine article：现在分词作后置定语
"配文插图" 是固定搭配 the graphic __(31)__ a magazine article was drawn by a person or a computer——graphic accompanying a magazine article 即 "配在杂志文章旁的插图"，accompany 与 graphic/article 是新闻出版中的常规搭配。
E)evoking"唤起一篇文章" 搭配不成立 evoking 是 "唤起、引发"，搭配对象多是 emotion/memory 等抽象名词；evoke a magazine article（唤起一篇杂志文章）语义不通，逻辑上也不是 "插图与文章" 的关系。
D) entertaining形容词
and 并列形容词链：relevant, new and __
读者期待 "贴题、新颖、有趣" 三件套 they just want it to be relevant, new and perhaps __(32)__.——读者作为大众，对杂志插图的诉求是 relevant（与文章相关）、new（新鲜）、entertaining（有趣）这三件套，构成同色彩并列；perhaps 又留了余地，正合 "有趣" 这种偏锦上添花的属性。
H)intuitive"直觉的" 与并列项不同色彩 intuitive 偏认知/操作领域（如 intuitive interface 易上手的界面），与读者读杂志插图时的诉求错位；与 relevant、new 也无法构成同色彩并列。
F) hybrid名词
a + __ 单数可数名词位

where 从句直接定义 "人机混合" Many fields will be a __(33)__, where some humans find a lucky place, but most of the work is done by computers, like in manufacturing today, where much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines.——where 从句里 "some humans … but most of the work is done by computers" 把空名词定义成 "人机混合体"，hybrid 是唯一精准对应词。
G)impetus"推动力" 与 "人机混合" 错位 impetus 是 "推动力、动力"，无法被 where 从句中 "既有人又有计算机" 的描述合理修饰；"许多领域将成为一种推动力" 在语义上也不通。
J) oversee动词
must be there to + 动词原形

"机器为主、人来监管" 正是本段图景 much of the work is accomplished by robots, but some humans must be there to __(34)__ the machines. 转折 but 之后明确：活儿主要由机器人干，但仍要有人 "在场"——"在场对机器" 干什么？最贴合的就是 "监督、监管" oversee，与制造业现实经验也一致。

M)surpass"超越机器" 与本段 "人辅助机器" 逻辑反向 surpass（超越）会把句意变成 "人必须在场以超越机器"，与 but 引出的 "机器为主、人为辅" 的图景反向；况且 surpass 已是 28 题的答案。 O)vanish不及物动词不能带 machines vanish 是不及物动词（消失），其后不能直接接 the machines 作宾语；语义上 "人必须在那里以消失机器" 也不通。
O) vanish动词
cause more jobs to + 动词原形

AI 会让更多工作消失，对应全段悲观预测 advances in AI will cause more jobs to __(35)__, that creative workers with human-only skills will become richer but fewer in number——后半 "人类技能工作者会变少" 直接揭示前半 "更多工作 __" 的方向是 "消失"，vanish 正中靶心。

longreading.title: 2025年12月·第2套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Projects, relationships, and jobs don't always work out as planned — and it's not always clear when to give up. We've all repeatedly heard the saying that "quitters never win", but sometimes the best decision is to cut our losses.
passages.zh: 项目、关系和工作并不总能按计划发展，而什么时候该放弃也并不总是显而易见。我们反复听到“放弃者永远不会获胜”这句话，但有时，及时止损才是最好的决定。

passages.en: B) Think about that relationship you held on to even after it had run its course or the job you stayed in despite your boss making you miserable. Many of us try to hold onto the last ray of hope, thinking we can make it work, whatever "it" is. And while perseverance is generally an excellent quality, it may also incline you to over-invest in something that is no longer a good idea.
passages.zh: 想想那段已经走到尽头、你却仍然坚持维系的关系，或者即使老板让你痛苦不堪、你却仍然留任的工作。我们中的许多人都试图抓住最后一线希望，认为无论“它”是什么，我们都能让它行得通。尽管坚持通常是一种很优秀的品质，但它也可能使你倾向于在某件已经不再明智的事情上投入过多。

passages.en: C) As an executive coach, I work with numerous passionate and hard-working leaders who don't want to "quit". But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't.
passages.zh: 作为一名高管教练，我与许多充满热情、勤奋努力且不愿“放弃”的领导者共事。但最明智的领导者懂得辨别过早放弃与坚持不该继续坚持的事情之间的区别。

passages.en: D) We are all susceptible to the sunk-cost delusion, an unconscious bias that leads us to persist in an endeavor we have already invested time, effort, or money into — even when abandoning it would be more beneficial. We realize that we can't get back the resources we've given, so we persevere — investing in a project that should be halted, staying in a relationship that should be over, or finishing a book we no longer enjoy and should put down, because we're already halfway through it. If quitting is "not your thing", you may be especially susceptible to this bias.
passages.zh: 我们都容易陷入沉没成本谬误，这是一种无意识的偏见，会导致我们持续投入一项已经耗费了时间、精力或金钱的事业，即使放弃它会更有益。我们意识到已经投入的资源无法收回，于是便继续坚持：继续投资于本应叫停的项目，维持一段本应结束的关系，或者因为一本书已经读了一半，便把一本自己已不再喜欢、其实应该放下的书读完。如果放弃“不是你的风格”，你可能尤其容易受到这种偏见的影响。

passages.en: E) The sunk-cost delusion causes us to overly worry about what we'll lose if we move on and not think enough about the costs of not moving on. To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. Ask yourself: What might I gain by cutting my losses now? Will you be happier or have time for another (better) opportunity? Then ask yourself: What will it cost me to soldier on? For example, is it possible that you'll be throwing more good money after what you've already lost? Or that you won't have the energy to capitalize on other promising possibilities?
passages.zh: 沉没成本谬误会使我们过度担心继续前进将失去什么，却没有充分考虑不继续前进的代价。为了抵消这种偏见，有意识地把思考重点重新放在收益上，这样你就能更客观地权衡各种选择。问问自己：现在及时止损，我可能得到什么？你会更快乐，或者有时间去把握另一个（更好的）机会吗？然后再问自己：继续坚持下去会让我付出什么代价？例如，你是否可能把更多的好钱投入到已经损失的钱之后？或者你会因此没有精力去利用其他有希望的可能性？

passages.en: F) The illusion of control can also interfere with our best judgment, leading us to overestimate our ability to control events and attain a positive outcome. This bias gives us a sense of agency and can promote mental health. However, the bias can also result in escalating commitment to a losing course of action. Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.
passages.zh: 控制幻觉也会干扰我们做出最佳判断，使我们高估自己控制事件和取得积极结果的能力。这种偏见会给我们带来一种能动感，也有助于促进心理健康。然而，这种偏见也可能导致我们对一条正在失败的行动路线投入越来越多。尤其是当它与“我不是一个会放弃的人”的心态结合在一起时，觉得自己对某个事件或某个人拥有比实际更多的控制力，就会使我们面临本该退出却反而加倍投入的风险。

passages.en: G) To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not. Think rigorously. While you may be able to influence other people and various circumstances, you can't force them to change or go your way.
passages.zh: 为了抵消这种偏见，审视你的处境，并简单列出两栏：哪些事情在你的控制范围内，哪些不在。务必严谨思考。虽然你或许能够影响他人和各种情况，但你无法强迫他们改变，也无法强迫事情按照你的意愿发展。

passages.en: H) Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. With a written list in hand, you can ensure you focus on what you can control and better assess whether your continued efforts are worth the expense. Expending effort and emotion on things you can't control can be both draining and disempowering.
passages.zh: 明确哪些事情你能控制、哪些事情你不能控制，对于判断究竟该放弃还是坚持至关重要。有了书面清单，你就能确保把注意力集中在自己能够控制的事情上，并更好地评估继续努力是否值得付出代价。把精力和情感耗费在无法控制的事情上，既会让人疲惫，也会使人感到无力。

passages.en: I) Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status.
passages.zh: 研究表明，人们会把自我认同和社会地位与自己的承诺联系起来。而且，由于我们会认同自己的承诺，退出其中一项承诺可能会让我们觉得自己的身份或地位受到了威胁。

passages.en: J) Take my client Ryan, a leader at a technology company. Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. As Ryan and I explored whether she should cancel the initiative she'd been leading or continue to persevere, she stated, "The thing is, I'm not a quitter." This singular, fixed sense of self was clouding her judgment and limiting her choices for action.
passages.zh: 以我的客户瑞安为例，她是一家科技公司的领导者。瑞安在一个没有带来所需成果的设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但想到要在投入了这么多之后放弃它，她就难以承受。当瑞安和我一起探讨她是否应该取消自己一直领导的这项计划，还是继续坚持时，她说：“问题在于，我不是一个会放弃的人。”这种单一而固定的自我认知蒙蔽了她的判断，也限制了她采取行动的选择。

passages.en: K) Our self-concept and identity are mental concepts that influence our behavior. If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. To overcome this kind of internal obstacle, recall your other positive traits and personality characteristics. Ask yourself: What additional strengths do I have (or aspire to have) that would be helpful to employ here? For example, when I asked Ryan what other positive qualities from her personality she needed to leverage for decision making, she replied, "Discernment and bravery."
passages.zh: 我们的自我概念和身份认同都是会影响行为的心理概念。如果你强烈认同自己不是一个会放弃的人，最终可能会因为狭隘而僵化的自我概念，困在某条行动道路上。要克服这种内在障碍，回想一下自己的其他积极特质和人格特点。问问自己：我还具备哪些（或希望具备哪些）可以帮助我处理眼前问题的优势？例如，当我问瑞安，她还需要调动自己性格中的哪些积极品质来帮助决策时，她回答说：“判断力和勇气。”

passages.en: L) Now, examine your situation through the lens of each of these facets of yourself. What does the discerning part of you say? The brave part? Considering your decision through these different characteristics will enable you to see that you have more choices. It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.
passages.zh: 现在，透过你自身这些不同特质的视角来审视自己的处境。你具有判断力的那一面会怎么说？勇敢的那一面呢？从这些不同特质出发思考你的决定，会让你意识到自己其实有更多选择。寻求外部信息来源也很有帮助，而不是只依赖自己的想法和直觉。但重要的是，要认真考虑你应该征求哪些人的意见。

passages.en: M) Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. If you're considering whether to shut down your entrepreneurial venture, for instance, reach out to other founders as opposed to just your business partner. Similarly, if you're looking for love advice, ask someone removed from the ups and downs of your relationship instead of relying only on your best friend. In all cases, I recommend describing your situation and following up with a question like: "How would you manage this situation?"
passages.zh: 理想情况下，应当寻找那些对你的决定投入程度不如你的人。例如，如果你正在考虑是否关闭自己的创业项目，可以联系其他创业者，而不是只询问你的商业伙伴。同样，如果你在寻求恋爱建议，也应该询问一个置身于你们关系起伏之外的人，而不是只依赖你最好的朋友。在所有情况下，我都建议你先描述自己的处境，然后提出类似这样的问题：“如果是你，你会如何处理这种情况？”

passages.en: N) Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. Sticking with the example of the entrepreneurial venture, numbers are your best friend. Use them to remove yourself from the love you have for this idea and consider your burn rate relative to growth plan, industry growth rates, and other factors that predict start-up success. External sources of information can help you see angles and possibilities you might not have considered.
passages.zh: 或者，你也可以寻找能够揭示你所考虑的事业真正成功概率的可靠数据。继续以创业项目为例，数字是你最好的朋友。利用数字，让自己暂时抽离对这一想法的喜爱，并考察你的资金消耗速度与增长计划、行业增长率以及其他能够预测初创企业成功的因素之间的关系。外部信息来源可以帮助你看到自己可能没有考虑过的角度和可能性。

passages.en: O) When something that seemed so promising at the start doesn't turn out the way we imagined, we can become overly self-critical. Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. The most effective strategy here is to give yourself a break. Practicing self-compassion increases your resilience(韧性), emotional intelligence, compassion toward others, and can boost your performance as well as help you develop a growth mindset.
passages.zh: 当一开始看起来如此有希望的事情最终没有像我们想象的那样发展时，我们可能会过度自我批评。没有人喜欢承认自己做出了糟糕的决定，尤其是当你高度重视明智决策这一品质时。这里最有效的策略是放自己一马。练习自我关怀能够增强你的韧性、情商和对他人的同情心，还能提升你的表现，并帮助你培养成长型思维。

passages.en: P) Instead of deliberating and criticizing yourself, focus instead on what you can learn from this situation. For example, Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project. And despite ultimately deciding to drop it, she was still happy she had tried and grateful for what the experience taught her.
passages.zh: 不要反复琢磨并批评自己，而应专注于从这段经历中学到什么。例如，瑞安意识到，在领导这个设计项目的过程中，她培养了各种新的技能和领导能力。尽管她最终决定放弃这个项目，但她仍然很高兴自己曾经尝试过，也很感激这段经历带给她的教益。

passages.en: Q) Undeniably, perseverance can help us succeed. But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action. While letting go can be difficult, it will free up your time, energy, and mental space to imagine new possibilities and pursue new opportunities.
passages.zh: 不可否认，坚持能够帮助我们取得成功。但为了你的身心健康，学会区分过早放弃和执着于一条正在失败的道路十分重要。尽管放手可能很困难，但它会释放你的时间、精力和心理空间，让你能够想象新的可能性并追求新的机会。

statements.en: Feeling like they have more control over something or someone than they do, people get more committed to their pursuit when they should give up.
statements.zh: 当人们感觉自己对某事或某人的控制力比实际情况更强时,他们会在本应放弃的时候对追求变得更加执着。

analysis.锚点: 高估掌控感导致继续投入
analysis.定位: F 段 Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out. 尤其当与"我不是放弃者"的心态结合时，觉得自己对某件事或某个人有比实际更多的掌控感，会让我们在本该退出时反而加码投入。
analysis.改写: Feeling like they have more control over something or someone than they do↔feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do 代词与名词的同义替换 get more committed to their pursuit when they should give up↔doubling down when we should pull out 口语短语的解释式改写

statements.en: If you regard yourself as one who never quits, you may end up trapped in your course of action.
statements.zh: 如果你把自己看作一个从不放弃的人,你可能最终会被困在自己的行动路线中。

analysis.锚点: 自认从不放弃者会被困住
analysis.定位: K 段 If you strongly identify as not being a quitter, you can end up staying stuck in a course of action due to your narrow and rigid self-concept. 如果你强烈地把自己认同为不是一个放弃者，那么你会因为狭隘僵化的自我概念，最终被困在某一行动路线里。
analysis.改写: If you regard yourself as one who never quits↔If you strongly identify as not being a quitter 动词与短语同义替换 trapped in your course of action↔staying stuck in a course of action 近义动词同义替换
analysis.辨邻: F F段出现了I'm not a quitter这一相同表述，容易让人误以为是源头段；但它的核心论点是控制错觉与该心态叠加导致doubling down，并不是题干所说的trapped in your course of action。 Especially when combined with an "I'm not a quitter" mentality, feeling like we have more control over an event or person than we do puts us at risk of doubling down when we should pull out.

statements.en: One of the author's clients found it hard to give up a design project, in which she had put in a lot of time and effort.
statements.zh: 作者的一位客户发现很难放弃一个设计项目,她在这个项目上投入了大量时间和精力。

analysis.锚点: 客户与设计项目的难放手
analysis.定位: J 段 Ryan had invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project that wasn't delivering the needed outcomes, but the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear. Ryan在一个迟迟拿不出预期成果的设计项目上投入了两年时间和大量精力，但一想到要在投入这么多之后放弃它就难以承受。
analysis.改写: One of the author's clients↔my client Ryan 专名与泛指对应 found it hard to give up a design project↔the thought of abandoning it after all she had put in was hard to bear 形容词短语同义替换 in which she had put in a lot of time and effort↔invested two years and a lot of effort in a design project 具体时长概括为时间
analysis.辨邻: P P段同样提到leading the design project，但内容是Ryan从中获得new skills and leadership capabilities并感激这段经历；它叙述的是后续学习与释怀，不是题干强调的found it hard to give up这一时刻。 Ryan recognized she had developed various new skills and leadership capabilities from leading the design project.

statements.en: The author suggests that one should direct their thoughts to the gains of quitting timely so as to move on.
statements.zh: 作者建议人们应该将思绪转向及时放弃所能获得的收益,以便继续前进。

analysis.锚点: 把思考转向及时放弃的收益
analysis.定位: E 段 To offset this bias, deliberately refocus your thinking on the gains so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives. 为抵消这一偏差，要刻意把思考重心转向收益，这样你才能更客观地权衡各种选择。
analysis.改写: direct their thoughts to the gains↔refocus your thinking on the gains 动词与名词同义替换 the gains of quitting timely↔What might I gain by cutting my losses now? 及时止损的同义表达 so as to move on↔so you can more objectively weigh the alternatives 目的状语的概括式改写

statements.en: When making a decision, you'd better ask for opinions of those who have less stake in your decision.
statements.zh: 在做决定时,你最好征求那些在你的决定中利益关系较小的人的意见。

analysis.锚点: 向利益相关度低的人征询
analysis.定位: M 段 Ideally, seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are. 理想情况下，要找那些比你在这项决定中投入度更低的人征询意见。
analysis.改写: ask for opinions of those who have less stake in your decision↔seek out people who are less invested in your decision than you are 动词与利益关系词同义
analysis.辨邻: L L段只说seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts并提示要think through whose opinions you solicit，把谁来征询这一具体回答推到下一段；它没有less stake这层意思，因此不是源头段。 It's also helpful to seek external sources of information, rather than relying solely on your thinking and instincts. But it's important to think through whose opinions you solicit.

statements.en: For people associating their identity with their commitments, quitting can feel like their identity is threatened.
statements.zh: 对于那些将身份认同与承诺联系在一起的人来说,放弃可能会让他们感觉自己的身份认同受到了威胁。

analysis.定位: I 段 Research indicates that people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments. And because we identify with our commitments, withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status. 研究表明，人们会把自我认同与社会地位与自己的承诺挂钩。正因为我们把自己等同于这些承诺，退出其中一项就会让人觉得像是对身份或地位的威胁。
analysis.改写: associating their identity with their commitments↔people link their self-identity and social status to their commitments 动词同义替换 quitting can feel like their identity is threatened↔withdrawing from one can feel like a threat to our identity or status 动名词被动改写

statements.en: People who regard highly the quality of making wise decisions do not feel good when they make a bad one.
statements.zh: 高度重视做出明智决策这一品质的人在做出错误决定时不会感觉良好。

analysis.锚点: 看重明智决策者面对坏决定的感受
analysis.定位: O 段 Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision, especially if making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem. 没有人喜欢觉得自己做了一个糟糕的决定，尤其当你把做出明智决定视为自己很看重的品质时。
analysis.改写: regard highly the quality of making wise decisions↔making intelligent decisions is a quality you hold in high esteem 动词短语与形容词同义 do not feel good when they make a bad one↔Nobody likes to feel that they've made a poor decision 否定改写+近义形容词

statements.en: The wisest leaders learn to distinguish between giving up too soon and sticking with something irrationally.
statements.zh: 最明智的领导者学会区分过早放弃和非理性地坚持某事。

analysis.锚点: 最聪明领导者懂得分辨
analysis.定位: C 段 But the smartest leaders learn to discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't. 但最聪明的领导者会学着分辨过早放弃与不该坚持却继续坚持之间的差别。
analysis.改写: The wisest leaders↔the smartest leaders 近义形容词最高级 distinguish between giving up too soon and sticking with something irrationally↔discern the difference between quitting too soon and holding onto something that they shouldn't 动词与短语的同义概括
analysis.辨邻: Q Q段出现learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action这一与题干高度相似的并置，是最容易让人误选的相邻段；但它谈的对象是普遍意义的人，并未限定The wisest leaders这一主语，故不是源头段。 But for your well-being, it's important to learn how to distinguish quitting too soon and clinging to a losing course of action.

statements.en: When people are thinking of an endeavor, they should dig out reliable data that tells them how likely they are to succeed.
statements.zh: 当人们考虑一项事业时,他们应该挖掘能够告诉他们成功可能性有多大的可靠数据。

analysis.锚点: 用可靠数据评估成功概率
analysis.定位: N 段 Alternately, you could also seek out hard data that illuminates your real chance of success in whatever endeavor you are contemplating. 或者，你也可以去寻找能够照亮你成功真实概率的硬数据，无论你在考虑哪种事业。
analysis.改写: dig out reliable data↔seek out hard data 动词与形容词同义 how likely they are to succeed↔your real chance of success 名词短语改写为从句 When people are thinking of an endeavor↔in whatever endeavor you are contemplating 近义动词替换

statements.en: Having a clear view of what's in your control and what's not is vital to making a good decision regarding whether to give up or stick it out.
statements.zh: 清楚地了解什么在你的控制范围内、什么不在你的控制范围内,对于就是否放弃还是坚持做出正确决定至关重要。

analysis.锚点: 看清可控与否对决策至关重要
analysis.定位: H 段 Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't is essential to making a quality decision about whether to call it quits or persevere. 把自己能控制什么、不能控制什么搞清楚，对于做出关于该放弃还是该坚持的高质量决定至关重要。
analysis.改写: Having a clear view of what's in your control and what's not↔Getting clear on what you can control and what you can't 动名词短语同义 vital to making a good decision↔essential to making a quality decision 近义形容词同义 whether to give up or stick it out↔whether to call it quits or persevere 并置短语整体同义
analysis.辨邻: G G段聚焦工具：make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not；它没有vital to making a good decision这层论点，因此不是源头段。 To counteract this bias, consider your situation and make a simple two-column list of what's in your control and what's not.

passages.en: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.
passages.zh: 作为相互依存的存在，我们无法脱离他人而蓬勃发展。我们喜欢与志趣相投的人一起工作，与他们共享共同的兴趣，或者他们也相信我们所认真对待的事业。这一点从我们将自己组织成各种集体群体中便可明显看出，例如国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭。

passages.en: Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
passages.zh: 你所属的群体是否具有强烈的集体意识或共同信念？其成员之间是否存在相互依存关系？你是否认为这个群体是你生命中重要的一部分？如果你的回答是肯定的，那么你正在经历一种微观层面的团结。

passages.en: What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."
passages.zh: 什么是团结？词典中最简单的定义是：“一群人之间统一的意见、感情、目标或利益。”

passages.en: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
passages.zh: 在我们所生活的这个日益多元化的社会中，团结呈现出复杂而多面的特征，因为它在生活于快速变化环境中的独特个体之间建立起相互依存的纽带，而这些个体又在复杂的劳动分工体系中工作。

passages.en: One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
passages.zh: 团结的一个方面与社群主义的原则十分契合。在这种情况下，个人放弃自身利益，以服务于共同利益。然而，对社会凝聚力和排他性的严格坚持，限制了个人差异和偏好的表达与实践。因此，为了维护群体的统一，个性和自主性被牺牲了。

passages.en: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
passages.zh: 团结也被视为对极端强调个人主义和选择自由的一种反应。它反对自由主义关于不受约束的个人的理念，这种理念认为社会妨碍了个人作出选择并按照对自己有利的方式行事，而不管这些选择和行为将如何影响他人。

passages.en: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.
passages.zh: 但是，尽管团结具有许多不同的层面，社会理论家仍将其视为促成社会秩序与进步的关键因素。他们认为，随着人类社会变得更加多元化，要使其得以存续，就需要基于差异建立更多新的纽带。鉴于此，他们认为真正的团结不仅仅是建立在共同利益之上的浅层关系。团结并不只是对某种行为将使自我获益多少进行战略计算的产物。它也不是建立在“你我对抗全世界”原则之上的排他性阶层。相反，它具有包容性，并非强迫形成。出于团结而行动，意味着相互支持、彼此挺身而出——承认一个人的命运与他人的命运息息相关。团结是一种以合作实践为特征的纽带，并因对他人福祉或共同利益的关切而得到加强。它为保护人的尊严而斗争，倾听最脆弱群体的呼声，并对此采取行动。

questions.stem: What does the author say about human beings?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对人类有何看法?

options.text: They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other.
options.zh: 他们若不相互合作就无法繁荣发展。

options.text: They share a common interest and believe in a just cause.
options.zh: 他们有共同的利益并相信正义的事业。

options.text: They think and behave alike in different social groups.
options.zh: 他们在不同社会群体中的思维和行为方式相似。

options.text: They cannot gain independence without fighting for it.
options.zh: 他们若不为之抗争就无法获得独立。

questions.判型: What does the author say about human beings? 问的是作者就 human beings 这一具体对象说了什么，落点在某一具体陈述上而非整篇主旨。
questions.拆句: What does the author say about human beings? 是常规疑问句结构，主干 "the author say"，关于 human beings，无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. 作为相互依赖的存在，我们无法脱离他人独自繁荣兴盛。

locate.en: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.
locate.zh: 作为相互依赖的存在，我们无法脱离他人独自繁荣兴盛。

option_analysis.note: They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other. 把 cannot thrive independent of others 改写为"必须合作才能兴旺"，正是预判内容的同义转述。

pairs.opt: cannot prosper without cooperating with each other

option_analysis.note: They share a common interest and believe in a just cause. 取自 we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about，但原文这是"喜欢和谁一起工作"的举例，不是对 human beings 的总体陈述；且 cause 被偷换为 just cause（正义事业）。
They think and behave alike in different social groups. 声称"在不同群体中想法行为都一样"，原文只说人喜欢和"like-minded"的人共事，并未说人在所有群体中思想行为都相同。
They cannot gain independence without fighting for it. 谈"独立要靠斗争争取"，但原文 we cannot thrive independent of others 强调的是"无法独立"而非"为独立而战"，话题相反。

questions.stem: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society?
questions.stem_zh: 关于日益多元化社会中的团结,我们了解到什么?

options.text: It gives rise to a complicated division of labor.
options.zh: 它引发了复杂的劳动分工。

options.text: It involves many aspects with great complexity.
options.zh: 它涉及许多具有高度复杂性的方面。

options.text: It brings individuals together as environment changes.
options.zh: 它随着环境变化将个体凝聚在一起。

options.text: It embraces the characteristics of different individuals.
options.zh: 它包容不同个体的特征。

questions.判型: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society? 提问限定在"多元化社会下的 solidarity"这一局部，并非整篇主旨。
questions.拆句: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society? 主干 "we learn about solidarity"，介词短语 "in an increasingly diverse society" 限定语境，无难句结构。
questions.定位: P4 In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor. 在我们所处的这个日益多元化的社会里，solidarity 呈现出复杂而多面的特征，因为它在快速变化的环境中、在复杂的分工内部，于各不相同的个体之间形成了相互依赖的纽带。

locate.en: In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
locate.zh: 在我们所处的这个日益多元化的社会里，solidarity 呈现出复杂而多面的特征，因为它在快速变化的环境中、在复杂的分工内部，于各不相同的个体之间形成了相互依赖的纽带。

option_analysis.note: It gives rise to a complicated division of labor. 说 solidarity 导致了复杂分工，但原文 working within a complex division of labor 是说 solidarity 发生"在"复杂分工"之内"，分工是背景而非结果。
involves many aspects with great complexity 同时覆盖原文的 complex 和 multifaceted 两个核心修饰语，且未做任何额外延伸。

pairs.orig: takes on a complex and multifaceted character
pairs.opt: involves many aspects with great complexity

option_analysis.note: It brings individuals together as environment changes. 把"形成相互依赖纽带"窄化为"把个体聚拢"，且偷换了主线——题干问的是"我们关于 solidarity 在多元社会中学到什么"，正确答案应概括其"特征"，C 选了一处细节当主答。
It embraces the characteristics of different individuals. 说 solidarity"接纳"个体差异，但原文只说它在 unique individuals 之间形成纽带，并未说它"接纳"或"包含"个体特征。

questions.stem: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism?
questions.stem_zh: 在社群主义的背景下我们会看到什么?

options.text: Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality.
options.zh: 社会规范的统治和个性的消除。

options.text: Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences.
options.zh: 强调坚持个体差异。

options.text: Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good.
options.zh: 为了公共利益而牺牲个人利益。

options.text: Elimination of individualism and personal choices.
options.zh: 消除个人主义和个人选择。

questions.判型: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism? 问的是该情境下会观察到什么，指向文中具体描述句。
questions.拆句: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism? 主干 "we would witness"，"in the setting of communitarianism" 限定情境，would 表示一般陈述语气，无难点。
questions.定位: P5 In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. 在这种情境下，个人放弃自身利益以服务于共同利益。

locate.en: In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.
locate.zh: 在这种情境下，个人放弃自身利益以服务于共同利益。

option_analysis.note: Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality. 把"个体在某情境下放弃个人利益"夸大为"社会规范统治、个性被彻底清除"，原文虽提到 individuality 被牺牲，但用的是 sacrificed（让位）而非 ridding（彻底清除）。

Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences. 说社群主义强调坚持个体差异，但原文 strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences 明说它限制了个体差异的表达，完全相反。
Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good. 是对 individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good 的完整、保守的名词化改写，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.orig: individuals give up their own interests

option_analysis.note: Elimination of individualism and personal choices. 用 Elimination（彻底消除）描述社群主义的效果，但原文只说 individuality and autonomy are sacrificed（让位/牺牲），并未达到"彻底消除"的程度。

questions.stem: What does solidarity entail according to the passage?
questions.stem_zh: 根据文章,团结意味着什么?

options.text: A limit to personal differences.
options.zh: 对个人差异的限制。

options.text: An opposition to individualism.
options.zh: 对个人主义的反对。

options.text: A hindrance to social advancement.
options.zh: 对社会进步的阻碍。

options.text: An inevitable end to liberal pursuits.
options.zh: 自由主义追求的必然终结。

questions.判型: What does solidarity entail according to the passage? 询问 solidarity 本质内涵，对应文中明确陈述句。
questions.拆句: What does solidarity entail according to the passage? 标准疑问句，谓语动词 entail 是关键考词，"according to the passage" 为状语，结构简单。
questions.定位: P6 Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. solidarity 也被视为对极端强调个人主义与选择自由的一种反应（反对）。

locate.en: Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.
locate.zh: solidarity 也被视为对极端强调个人主义与选择自由的一种反应（反对）。

option_analysis.note: A limit to personal differences. 来自 restricts expression and practice of individual differences，那是讲社群主义的代价，不是讲 solidarity 整体的内涵；题干问的是 solidarity entail 什么。
An opposition to individualism 是 a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism 最直接的同义改写，与预判一致。

pairs.orig: a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism
the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice

option_analysis.note: A hindrance to social advancement. 把 solidarity 说成"社会进步的障碍"，但原文 see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices 是说"自由派认为社会是其自由的障碍"，hindrance 的主语应为 society 而非 solidarity；并且 P7 明说 solidarity 是 order and progress 的关键。
An inevitable end to liberal pursuits. 说 solidarity 会"不可避免地终结"自由派追求，但原文只说它是对极端个人主义的 reaction（反对/回应），并未说会"终结"或必然成功，且 inevitable 加重了语气。

questions.stem: What do social theorists think of solidarity?
questions.stem_zh: 社会理论家如何看待团结?

options.text: It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable.
options.zh: 它与最弱势群体尤其相关。

options.text: It is most effective in protecting human dignity.
options.zh: 它在保护人类尊严方面最为有效。

options.text: It is essential to progress and order in society.
options.zh: 它对社会的进步与秩序至关重要。

options.text: It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships.
options.zh: 它对于避免肤浅关系不可或缺。

questions.判型: What do social theorists think of solidarity? 问的是 social theorists 这一具体群体的看法，定位明确，不是整篇作者主旨。
questions.拆句: What do social theorists think of solidarity? 主语 "social theorists"，think of 是固定搭配"看待/认为"，结构平铺直叙。
questions.定位: P7 But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. 但是，尽管 solidarity 有诸多面向，社会理论家们仍把它视为推动社会秩序与进步的关键因素。

locate.en: But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.
locate.zh: 但是，尽管 solidarity 有诸多面向，社会理论家们仍把它视为推动社会秩序与进步的关键因素。

option_analysis.note: It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable. 取自 listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable，原文这是对 solidarity 内涵的一种延伸描述，且"especially relevant"是干扰项的额外断言；题干问的是社会理论家对 solidarity 的整体看法，而非"它最关乎谁"。
It is most effective in protecting human dignity. 用 most effective（最有效）做绝对化判断，但原文 It fights for the protection of human dignity 仅说它"为人类尊严而战"，并未与其他事物比较"最有效"。
essential to progress and order in society 是 a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society 的标准同义改写，与预判完全对应。

pairs.orig: a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society
pairs.opt: essential to progress and order in society

pairs.orig: bringing about order and progress in society

option_analysis.note: It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships. 说 solidarity 对"避免肤浅关系"必不可少，但原文 they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests 是说"真正的 solidarity 不仅仅是肤浅关系"，是在界定 solidarity 本身，而非说它用于"避免肤浅关系"。

reading2.title: 2025年12月·第2套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
passages.zh: 反复提出他人不需要的建议的人可能是出于好意，也是真心想要帮忙。另一些人这样做，可能是因为他们从影响他人的能力中获得了自我价值感。一项研究发现，与具有相反倾向的人相比，权力寻求倾向较强的人更有可能提出建议。

passages.en: Under the guise(外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
passages.zh: 人们可能以无私为幌子，实际上是因为提出你不需要的建议会让他们感到自己有力量或能够掌控局面，才会这样做。不过，他们可能并没有充分意识到这种驱动力。

passages.en: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
passages.zh: 这些人还可能表现出程度较高且有问题的情绪脆弱性，很快变得不安，并且需要很长时间才能平静下来。他们的情绪或许只有在童年时期表现得最为激烈时才会得到认可，这促使他们养成了在大多数情况下都过度应对不适的方式。

passages.en: When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
passages.zh: 当一个人提出建议是为了让自己感到更有力量时，他们的行为背后存在一种焦虑，而接受建议的人往往能够察觉到这一点。在这种情况下，人们很容易严厉地回应提出建议的人，并指责他们是在操纵他人，但这种做法可能会产生不理想的结果。

passages.en: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
passages.zh: 如果提出建议这一行为正在积极地促成某人的自我价值感，那么直率的拒绝可能会被视为一种威胁，激活他们的战或逃反应，可能使他们进一步强化寻求认可的行为，或者导致更大的冲突。

passages.en: The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"
passages.zh: 关键在于给予认可，但不要过度认同。你可以让他们知道你听到了他们的话，也理解他们的出发点，同时不要接受那种可能有害的说法，即没有他们的帮助你就无法解决问题。你最好这样说：“谢谢你的建议。我有自己的计划来处理这件事，但我真的很感谢你的看法，也会考虑你的意见。以后我需要帮助时，可以告诉你吗？”

passages.en: If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.
passages.zh: 如果你难以以圆 tact 的方式设定界限，就应优先提升自己的自我调节能力。即使持续接受这些建议可能令人感到不适，只要你能够以同理心作出回应，局面很可能会更快缓和下来。

passages.en: Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
passages.zh: 尽管提出未经请求的建议通常并非为了达到这样的结果，但许多接受建议的人常常会因这些不需要的建议而感到压力、受到冒犯，或者仅仅感到恼火。如果你觉得有必要，在这方面设定界限完全合理，而且这能让你获得更强的情绪安全感。

passages.en: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
passages.zh: 设定界限时，最好考虑到对方这样做背后的原因，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

questions.stem: What is the finding of one study about people who keep giving unsolicited advice?
questions.stem_zh: 一项研究关于不断提供主动建议的人有什么发现?

options.text: They turn out to be well-meaning.
options.zh: 他们原来是出于好意的。

options.text: They are genuinely kind-hearted.
options.zh: 他们确实心地善良。

options.text: They are capable of influencing others.
options.zh: 他们有能力影响他人。

options.text: They are inclined to crave for power.
options.zh: 他们倾向于渴望权力。

questions.判型: 题干 What is the finding of one study 指向某个具体研究的事实性结论，不含 infer/imply/mainly。
questions.拆句: 题干主干是 What is the finding of one study，about 引导的介词短语修饰 finding，限定研究对象是 people who keep giving unsolicited advice（who 引导定语从句修饰 people）。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency. 一项研究发现，求权欲望强的人比求权欲望相反（低）的人更倾向于给出建议。

locate.en: One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
locate.zh: 一项研究发现，求权欲望强的人比求权欲望相反（低）的人更倾向于给出建议。

option_analysis.note: They turn out to be well-meaning 取自首句 can be well-meaning，但那只是 give advice 的一种可能动机的铺垫，并非“研究的发现”。
They are genuinely kind-hearted 改写自 genuinely want to help，同样位于铺垫句，不是研究结论。
They are capable of influencing others 把 self-worth around the ability to influence others 中“自我价值感来自影响他人的能力”误读为“具备影响他人能力”，且这同样不在 study 结论里。
四项中只有 inclined to crave for power 与预判“求权欲强者更爱给建议”形成 1:1 同义对应。

pairs.orig: a high tendency to seek power

questions.stem: What is the problem with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice?
questions.stem_zh: 那些被驱使向你提供主动建议的人有什么问题?

options.text: They may be quick to upset others.
options.zh: 他们可能很快就会让别人不高兴。

options.text: They may be emotionally vulnerable.
options.zh: 他们可能在情感上很脆弱。

options.text: They want their voice to be the loudest.
options.zh: 他们想让自己的声音最响亮。

options.text: They respond to discomfort excessively.
options.zh: 他们对不适过度反应。

questions.判型: 题干 What is the problem with 指向一个可在原文中找到具体描述的缺陷。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is the problem，介词短语 with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice 修饰 problem；who 引导被动语态定语从句。注意 driven 是被动，表示“被某种力量驱使”，而不是主动选择。
questions.定位: P3 These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. 这些人还可能表现出某种程度上有问题的情绪脆弱性——很快就情绪激动，且久久不能平复。

locate.en: These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.
locate.zh: 这些人还可能表现出某种程度上有问题的情绪脆弱性——很快就情绪激动，且久久不能平复。

option_analysis.note: They may be quick to upset others 把原文中“自己易激动”扭曲为“使他人易激动”——动作发出者由 these people 变成对他人施加影响。
预判的“情绪脆弱”在四项中只与 emotionally vulnerable 对应；A/C/D 都来自定位句的修饰部分。

pairs.orig: a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability

option_analysis.note: They want their voice to be the loudest 改自 their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest，那是对成因的猜测且发生在童年，并非“现在的问题”本身。
They respond to discomfort excessively 取自 adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations，那是脆弱情绪导致的“反应方式”，是表现/后果，而题干问的是“问题本身”。

questions.stem: What is the advice receiver tempted to do when noticing the advice giver's underlying anxiety?
questions.stem_zh: 当注意到建议提供者潜在的焦虑时,建议接受者会倾向于做什么?

options.text: Reveal the undesired result of their approach.
options.zh: 揭示他们的方法所带来的不良结果。

options.text: Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner.
options.zh: 以不加掩饰的方式拒绝他们的建议。

options.text: Bring their real motives to the surface.
options.zh: 将他们的真实动机揭露出来。

options.text: Accuse them of trying to control others.
options.zh: 指责他们试图控制他人。

questions.判型: 题干 What is the advice receiver tempted to do 指向一个原文中可直接对应的具体行为。
questions.拆句: 主干 What is the advice receiver tempted to do，when 引导时间状语从句 when noticing the advice giver’s underlying anxiety（noticing 为分词短语）。注意 tempted to do 不等于“已经做”，而是“被诱使想去做”。
questions.定位: P4 It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result. 在这种情况下，人很容易被诱使去强硬回怼劝告者并指责他们在操控自己，但这种做法可能导致不希望出现的结果。

locate.en: It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
locate.zh: 在这种情况下，人很容易被诱使去强硬回怼劝告者并指责他们在操控自己，但这种做法可能导致不希望出现的结果。

option_analysis.note: Reveal the undesired result of their approach 把原文 this approach might produce an undesired result 中“己方做法的结果”硬塞为“揭露对方做法的结果”，且 reveal 这一动作原文从未出现。
Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner 取自 an outright rejection 的 outright（直率的），属于 Q54 区间内容；与 Q53 问的“被诱使做什么”无关。
Bring their real motives to the surface 谈“把真实动机暴露出来”，原文虽提到 They may not be fully aware of this drive，但从未说被诱使去把动机带到台面上。
在 to react harshly 与 to accuse them of being manipulative 两个候选动作里，只有 Accuse them of trying to control others 与后者形成精确同义改写。

pairs.opt: Accuse them of trying to control others

questions.stem: How is the advice giver likely to react to the rejection of their advice?
questions.stem_zh: 建议提供者对他们的建议被拒绝可能会有什么反应?

options.text: They may regard it as a threat.
options.zh: 他们可能会将其视为一种威胁。

options.text: They may modify their behavior.
options.zh: 他们可能会改变自己的行为。

options.text: They get ready for a larger conflict.
options.zh: 他们为更大的冲突做好准备。

options.text: They begin to doubt their self-worth.
options.zh: 他们开始怀疑自己的自我价值。

questions.判型: 题干 How is the advice giver likely to react 问的是一个原文中有具体描述的反应方式。
questions.拆句: 主干 How is the advice giver likely to react，to 引导的介词短语 to the rejection of their advice 表反应对象。likely to 是预测性短语，对应原文的 may/possibly 等情态表达。
questions.定位: P5 If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict. 如果给建议这一行为正主动地构建着对方的自我价值感，那么一次直率的拒绝可能被对方视为威胁，激活其“战或逃”反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求认可，或引发更大的冲突。

locate.en: If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
locate.zh: 如果给建议这一行为正主动地构建着对方的自我价值感，那么一次直率的拒绝可能被对方视为威胁，激活其“战或逃”反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求认可，或引发更大的冲突。

option_analysis.note: 预判“视为威胁”在四项中只与 They may regard it as a threat 形成 1:1 同义对应；B/C/D 均取自定位句末尾的分词链或脱离原文。

pairs.opt: They may regard it as a threat

option_analysis.note: They may modify their behavior 暗示劝告者会调整行为；原文却是 double down on their validation-seeking behavior——加倍重复原行为，方向相反。
They get ready for a larger conflict 描述劝告者“准备好”打更大架；原文是 possibly...leading to a larger conflict，只是分词链中可能的下游结果，并非劝告者主动准备。
They begin to doubt their self-worth 说劝告者开始怀疑自己；原文方向相反——他们的 self-worth 被威胁后，会更努力地寻求认可（double down on validation-seeking），而不是怀疑。

questions.stem: What should the advice receiver do to avoid unnecessary conflict?
questions.stem_zh: 建议接受者应该怎么做才能避免不必要的冲突?

options.text: Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable.
options.zh: 承认该建议是完全合理的。

options.text: Give their reasons for not taking the advice.
options.zh: 给出他们不采纳该建议的理由。

options.text: Understand why the advice giver offers the advice.
options.zh: 理解建议提供者为什么要提供这个建议。

options.text: Explain their chosen way of handling the situation.
options.zh: 解释他们所选择的处理情况的方式。

questions.判型: 题干 What should the advice receiver do 指向作者给出的明确建议，文章末段往往有归纳。
questions.拆句: 主干 What should the advice receiver do，to 引导目的状语 to avoid unnecessary conflict。should 是关键情态动词，意味着答案对应文中明确的建议性陈述，而非可能性陈述。
questions.定位: P9 It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress. 最好以一种顾及当事人行为背后深层动机的方式来设界限，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

locate.en: It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
locate.zh: 最好以一种顾及当事人行为背后深层动机的方式来设界限，以避免不必要的冲突和更多压力。

option_analysis.note: Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable 让步承认建议合理，是放弃自己立场；原文是劝考者“自己设界限是 perfectly reasonable”，主语完全不同。
Give their reasons for not taking the advice 让 receiver 说出自己的拒绝理由；原文范本话术 I have my own plan for handling this 谈的是“我自有方案”，并未要求陈述拒绝理由，更不是 P9 给出的总策略。
预判“顾及对方深层动机”在四项中只与 Understand why the advice giver offers the advice 形成 1:1 同义对应。

pairs.orig: takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing
pairs.opt: Understand why the advice giver offers the advice

option_analysis.note: Explain their chosen way of handling the situation 描述 receiver 解释自己的处理方式，对应 I have my own plan for handling this 的示范话术之一，但题干问的是“避免冲突的做法”——文末 P9 的总结才是答案。

translation.title: 2025年12月·第2套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍中华民族自强自立精神及其成就 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 中华民族崇尚自强自立的精神，这一精神深植于中国文化之中，是民族生存与发展的重要支撑。改革开放以来，中国在自强自立的征程上，持续加大科研投入，在信息技术、人工智能、航天工程等领域不断取得新突破。5G 网络覆盖全国，远程医疗发展迅速，电子支付的使用全球领先，嫦娥探月工程展现了航天领域引人注目的发展。自强自主精神成为推动国家现代化进程的强大动力，激励着中国人民为实现民族复兴 (rejuvenation) 的中国梦不断奋进。
translation.reference_en:
The Chinese nation values the spirit of self-reliance and self-improvement, which is deeply rooted in Chinese culture and serves as a vital support for the survival and development of the nation. Since the reform and opening-up, China has continued to increase its investment in scientific research on its journey toward self-reliance, and has kept making new breakthroughs in such fields as information technology, artificial intelligence and aerospace engineering. For example, 5G networks now cover the whole country, telemedicine is developing rapidly, and electronic payment is used more widely than anywhere else in the world; the Chang'e lunar exploration program also demonstrates remarkable progress in China's aerospace field. The spirit of self-reliance and self-improvement has become a powerful driving force behind the country's modernization, inspiring the Chinese people to keep forging ahead toward the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.
【衔接】
第1句与第2句之间：从"是什么"过渡到"怎么做"首句讲精神"是什么"，第二句 改革开放以来 转入具体成就，时间状语 Since the reform and opening-up 天然起到承接作用，已交代背景切换，无须再额外加关联词，顺承即可。
第3句开头：与第2句"领域突破"的衔接第二句概括说"在各领域取得突破"，第三句是这些突破的具体例证。可在第三句前补一个承接词如 For example/Specifically，把"概括—举例"的逻辑显化：For example, 5G networks cover the whole country…，让读者看出第三句是在为第二句举证。
第3句末与第4句：从"成就"升华到"意义"第三句罗列成就、第四句升华到"成为动力、激励奋进"。第四句主语 The spirit of self-reliance 回扣首句主题，自然完成"成就—精神意义"的回环，前可不加关联词，靠主语复现承接即可，使全篇首尾呼应。
